events.title: What the Glass Threw Out
events.attendance_note: All four independent witnesses present under Iria Vale’s emergency charter.
events.opening_note: The Counterseal Witnesses enter a sealed museum scene while Dorr presses to classify the rupture as ordinary vandalism.

events.party_label: The Counterseal Witnesses with Iria Vale, Ors Renn, Ossa Pell, and Lio Marr

events.text: Mira and Ossa separate the answer-pin, theft tools, and destination evidence into three custody packets instead of treating the burst case as one undifferentiated scene.
Aven takes a counter-signed rubbing of the accession number; Renn seals the original shard and the missing-saw tray before Dorr can move them under an undocumented trustee order.
Lysa records Lio’s service-door sight line after Pell stabilizes the hanging case and clears glass from the docent’s path.

events.note: The restricted accession number makes the substitution ledger an actionable lead.
The bell-metal filings and chapel wax identify a workshop tied to the rupture, though the group does not yet know its full function.
The Vale carriage seal gives an immediate destination for direct pursuit.
Lio saw the wrapped weight enter the public court, where the transfer can be reconstructed from independent witnesses.
The copy backing identifies the west infirmary as an independent source for the original shrine and Olyra’s history.
Tavia’s missing numbered saw matches the cuts, making her the named theft suspect rather than merely the absent employee.

events.text: Renn holds the live answer-pin under watch seal; Ossa holds the saw tray; Aven carries a counter-signed accession rubbing outside trustee custody.

events.party_label: The Counterseal Witnesses with Sergeant Vela Rusk, Pellen Vey, Hara Bex, Iven Quill, and Sera Mott

events.text: The witnesses are interviewed separately: Pellen supplies weight, Hara supplies wax and wagon movement, and the copyists supply the argument and carriage handoff.
The group does not chase Tavia. Iven and Sera carry word to the House that the investigators will bring a certified record and evidence of a possible living cost.
Lysa asks the West Door families only to preserve their own observations; they withdraw their children from the front rank but make no promise to testify or accept custody.

events.note: Dorr’s summons identifies the chamber as the place where lawful scope and procession delay will be contested.
Tavia’s token identifies the House as her destination and the likely public-copy route.

events.text: Pellen, Hara, Iven, and Sera sign separate statements; the Vale-carriage allegation is public but remains disputed; the procession loses its West Door children from the front rank.

events.party_label: The Counterseal Witnesses with Senna Drail, Eren Sol, and Mave Kitt

events.text: Aven prioritizes the Olyra and modern-suppression packets. Eren certifies the deposition and survivor index while Mave certifies the trustee minute and recent conservation finding.
One certified set goes under Renn’s watch seal; one remains with the investigators for a public reading. Senna keeps every original and logs Dorr’s later suspension order.
The group deliberately leaves the ritual diagram packet unopened when Dorr’s order reaches the public stair; this preserves authentication but costs them the chapel-to-manor working details.

events.note: The memorandum confirms that the missing silver in the gallery is the object named by the old accession chain.
Olyra’s deposition directly states that she broke the council seal and opened the abandoned infirmary.
Alis’s warning establishes a real Vale voice hazard and city-wide transmission, but not yet the exact three-stage mechanism.

events.text: Two certified packets now exist outside Vale and museum control; Dorr’s signed suspension closes the public stair after their removal and enters Senna’s custody log.

events.closing_note: The witnesses have a theft route, a certified historical contradiction, and a living-voice warning, but no warrant, no counterkey, and no control of the sunset peal.

events.title: A Warrant Refused
events.attendance_note: All four independent witnesses present under Iria Vale’s emergency charter.
events.opening_note: The group brings certified evidence into the emergency trustee session while the procession resumes forming below the windows.

events.party_label: The Counterseal Witnesses with Helian Dorr, Iria Vale, Ors Renn, and the divided trustees

events.text: Dorr accepts that theft and concealment are proven but refuses a manor search and full procession delay, claiming the voice warning is too old and unspecific for private entry.
Renn obtains only a narrow belfry safety inspection. Dorr signs the refusal, preserves the full peal order, and orders petition copies held rather than destroyed.
Iria publicly acknowledges the false display and family custody but does not claim authority to surrender the heartglass or excuse Edrin.

events.note: The maintenance order identifies three unexplained Grand Belfry pins installed under Edrin’s authority.
The chamber procedure defines a same-day public entry and named custody plan that can survive another private promise.

events.text: Dorr denies the manor warrant and procession hold in writing, grants a narrow belfry inspection, preserves the full peal, and creates a signed public record of institutional refusal.

events.party_label: The Counterseal Witnesses with Nessa Quill, Tavia Sorn, and the four petition caucuses

events.text: Tavia reads Alis’s voice warning and rejects Edrin’s plan to take any Vale voice. She confesses sabotage, theft, and the carriage transfer without asking to be absolved.
Nessa sends certified copies through three named keepers and organizes a public reading outside Vale Manor. The Quiet Keepers retain one sealed copy rather than joining the march.
The most repeated current petition is “Open the doors,” but no one carries that packet into the winter garden. It becomes public language, not an automatic change to the vow-bed.

events.note: The copy ledgers show that the silver carries recurring, incompatible imperatives accumulated over decades.

events.text: Tavia cooperates under Renn’s named custody; three certified copy sets leave by different keepers; petitioners commit to a public reading outside the manor; no current petition packet is placed in the apparatus.

events.party_label: The Counterseal Witnesses with Jori Kest, Mela Fen, Rian Voss, Pavo Tern, Lis Aven, and Karel Venn

events.text: The group has no tuning strip and does not pretend otherwise. Pell and Kest identify the crown bell from Mela’s ledger and the pins’ separate resonance, then choose a manual rope bind instead of live-pin removal.
The narrow inspection order and Tavia’s confession give Kest enough cover for controlled work. Rian refuses to remove a pin but accepts a brake-post bind that can be inspected and later released.
Kest sounds the public warning pattern before binding the crown rope. Petitioners and watch move toward the west lawn; Dorr receives the warning only after it is audible city-wide.

events.note: Kest identifies exact bell operations, while the party’s missing counterkey limits them to binding rather than controlled pin removal or retuning.

events.text: The public warning peal sounds; the crown bell is manually bound at its brake post; witness and mouth bells remain operable; no stage pin is safely removed; Kest, Mela, and Rian become named witnesses.

events.closing_note: The manor warrant has failed, but certified copies, Tavia’s confession, a public-custody pledge, a warning peal, and a physically bound crown bell now exist as separate durable facts.

events.title: The Saint Who Could Not Answer
events.attendance_note: All four independent witnesses present under Iria Vale’s emergency charter.
events.opening_note: The Counterseal Witnesses approach Vale Manor behind a warning crowd while the witness bell remains ready and the crown bell is physically bound.

events.party_label: The Counterseal Witnesses with Iria Vale, Tavia Sorn, Ors Renn, Nessa Quill, Jori Kest, Edrin Vale, Leva Orm, and Peren Holt

events.text: The public approach supplies two independent anchors: certified copies already distributed outside and the warning crowd reading Olyra’s deposition. The group names interim custody before asking Edrin to stand down.
Tavia rejects the involuntary mouth stage in public; Iria acknowledges the Vale concealment; Kest certifies that the crown bell is bound but warns that the witness and mouth notes remain live.
Edrin moves to Witnessed Terms. He permits the witness note as a public demonstration, opens the garden doors, and agrees that no current petition packet will be placed on the vow-bed.

events.note: The witness body cannot recognize the fever doors and repeats a civic slogan instead of Olyra’s deposition; it is unstable evidence, not Olyra restored.

events.text: The witness note forms a translucent figure that recites “open the doors,” “wait for lawful order,” and unrelated pleas. It answers no question and recognizes no personal relic.
A witness-only Glass Saint forms before named observers; it provides no unknown fact, stable personality, or claim to be Olyra.
Edrin steps off the speaker mark and opens the inner mouth knot before the second note; no Vale voice is taken.
The manual crown-bell bind holds through the finale; no crown note launches and neither relay tower receives a command.
Peren lowers and seals the heartglass after the demonstration; the witness body collapses without broken panes or injured servants.
Edrin and Tavia submit to Renn’s named custody. Cooperation is recorded without erasing conspiracy, sabotage, injury, theft, or attempted compulsion.

Interim custody is split: Renn seals the inert heartglass; the House inventories and holds the vow-bed; Senna retains archive originals; certified copies remain distributed; the shrine panes stay shuttered under Leva’s household inventory pending a public hearing.

Olyra’s deposition and the trustee concealment minute receive a witnessed public reading and distributed certified copies, but no infirmary family testimony or physical hospice authentication has yet been obtained.
Dorr’s warrant denial, peal order, and prior concealment minute enter a public inquiry; the adventure does not recast him as an occult conspirator.

The obedience cult fractures publicly around the deposition and witness body; petition caucuses remain divided over relic preservation, prosecution, and whether any future answering rite should be attempted.

events.closing_note: Immediate coercion ends with no stolen voice and no command. The city has a public record, a witnessed but unstable manifestation, divided custody, named accused people, and unresolved arguments about Olyra, the relic, and institutional reform.
